Dec. 16 - Caramel secrets:
- Put 1/2 cup sugar plus 1 tbsp water in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1/8 tsp cream of tartar along with the sugar.
- Twirl as soon as the sugar starts melting and continue until all the dry sugar is dissolved or melted. Take care not to burn it during this step; browning happens after the sugar has melted/dissolved.
- When the solution starts to become reddish, turn down the flame and move the pan off the heat.
- Add 1/4 cup warm water to the pan. It will solidify on the bottom; put the pan back on the heat and swirl the liquid to dissolve/release the hardened caramel.
- Take care not to brown it too much. Take the pan off the heat and pour the liquid caramel into a heatproof container (mason jar or glass measuring cup).

Total quantity: two 8-inch loaf pans [8 x 2 1/2 x 3 1/2] and one 5-inch loaf pan [5.75 x 3 inches].

5/16/20 - 4 stars
- Needed a little more sauce in the onion gravy; a bit more water at the end would have done it.
- Also added 2 tsp tomato paste; can skip this next time.
- Did not add the sugar, but should have done so before adding the eggs.

Chettinad Egg Curry - 10/17, first attempt: Really good; will make again.
- Used 4 tsp tomato paste with 1 cup water instead of puree.
- Used only 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste; maybe should have used 1.5 tbsp.
- Next time slice the eggs in half and fry.
- Interesting flavor of vinegar and roasted coconut; it reminded me of the red chutney for dosa.
- Reduce Kashmiri chili powder to 1/2 tbsp.
- Reduce black peppercorn to 1/2 tbsp (used 1 tbsp).
- Took a long time to make: 1.5 hours.
- Ingredient annotation: 7 eggs, boiled for 10 minutes.

Chettinad Egg Curry continuation:
Attempt #2 (11/13) - 3/5, not so good.
1. Boiled eggs starting in cold water for 12 minutes over a medium-hot flame, with a rolling boil toward the end. Did not put the eggs into an ice bath immediately after cooking. Next time start the eggs in rolling boiling water for 12 minutes, ice-bath immediately, and use running water to peel if the shells are too sticky.
2. Roasted the coconut powder too much. It should only be heated lightly over a low flame for a nice aroma. Also possibly added too much coriander powder.
3. Added 6 tsp tomato paste to 1 1/2 cups water (possibly too much). Did not cook this down enough to sweeten the dish a bit.

Attempt #3 (11/15) - 3/5, not good.
1. Boiled 8 eggs in boiling water for 12 minutes and then immersed them in cold water. Peeling the shells was not too difficult.
2. Used frozen coconut; not sure there was much flavor because it was too wet to get dry enough by roasting. Stick with dry coconut next time.
3. Worst mistake: used canned tomato sauce. It was too acidic and had a strong vinegary flavor, which ruined the dish. Do not use canned sauce; stick with tomato paste and water.

[Date unclear] - 2 stars

- Dry-roasted the spices and ground them.
- Fried onions with ginger-garlic paste and green chilies.

- Cooked over medium-high heat for 1 hour, then simmered for 30 minutes after adding potatoes.

ingredients.rawText: 153 grams all-purpose flour (1 cup plus 1 tablespoon and 2 teaspoons)
ingredients.item: all-purpose flour (1 cup plus 1 tablespoon and 2 teaspoons)

instructions.text: Combine both flours and the salt in a large mixing bowl.

In a separate bowl, stir together about 200 grams (just under 1 cup) lukewarm water with the yeast and olive oil, then mix into the flour. Knead by hand for about 3 minutes, then let the dough rest for 15 minutes.

Knead the rested dough for another 3 minutes, then divide into two equal balls. Place on a floured surface, cover with a damp cloth, and let rise 3-4 hours at room temperature, or 8-24 hours in the refrigerator (bring refrigerated dough back to room temperature for 30-45 minutes before shaping).
Stretch each dough ball into a round or square on a floured surface using your fingers and hands, then top and bake. Yields two 12-inch pizzas.

R0334.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed directly against the recipe's NYT Cooking page (2026-08-30); instructions paraphrased, not copied verbatim.

ingredients.rawText: 2 1/2 pounds apples, peeled and cored, then cut into wedges (5 large honeycrisps will do it)
ingredients.item: apples, peeled and cored, then cut into wedges (5 large honeycrisps will do it)

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the apples, and stir to coat; cook, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, whisk together the spices, salt, and 3/4 cup sugar, then stir into the apples. Lower the heat and cook until the apples start to soften, about 5-7 minutes.

Sprinkle the flour and cornstarch over the apples and cook 3-5 minutes more. Remove from heat, stir in the cider vinegar, and scrape into a bowl to cool completely (spreading it on a rimmed baking sheet cools it faster).
Put a large baking sheet on the middle oven rack and preheat to 425°F. Roll one dough disc out on a floured surface into a roughly 12-inch round.
Fit that crust into a 9-inch pie plate leaving a 1/2-inch overhang, then freeze it. Roll the second dough disc into a 10-11 inch round.
Remove the chilled crust from the freezer, add the cooled apple filling, and cover with the second round of dough.
Press the edges together, trim the excess, crimp with a fork, and cut a few steam vents in the top crust.
Brush the top with the beaten egg and sprinkle with the remaining tablespoon of sugar.

Bake on the hot baking sheet at 425°F for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375°F and continue baking 30-40 minutes more, until bubbling and golden brown. Cool on a rack about 2 hours before slicing.

ingredients.rawText: 3 sticks/340 grams cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes
ingredients.item: cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes

ingredients.rawText: 3/4 cup/75 grams walnuts, toasted and chopped
1 1/2 pounds/680 grams tart apples, such as Granny Smith (about 3 large), peeled, cored and cut into 1/8-inch slices
ingredients.item: tart apples, such as Granny Smith (about 3 large), peeled, cored and cut into 1/8-inch slices

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 pounds/680 grams sweet-tart apples, such as Fuji, Pink Lady or Gala (about 3 large), peeled, cored and cut into 1/8-inch slices
ingredients.item: sweet-tart apples, such as Fuji, Pink Lady or Gala (about 3 large), peeled, cored and cut into 1/8-inch slices

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Line a 9-by-13-inch cake pan with foil, overhanging the sides, and grease lightly with softened butter.

Pulse the flour, sugar and salt in a food processor. Add the cold butter and pulse until it resembles coarse sand. Set aside 1 1/2 cups of this mixture in a bowl and work in the walnuts, cinnamon and cardamom; squeeze together into a rough dough ball (some crumbly bits are fine) and refrigerate.
Press the remaining crust mixture evenly into the bottom of the pan and about 1/2 inch up the sides.
Bake the crust until golden and dry to the touch, 20-25 minutes. Cool on a rack, then raise the oven temperature to 375°F.

While the crust bakes, toss the apples with the lemon juice. Melt the butter in a large sauté pan over medium-high heat, add the cinnamon, nutmeg and cardamom and cook about 15 seconds, then add the apples and cook, stirring often, until just starting to soften, about 5 minutes. Stir in the sugar and continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until the released juices evaporate and the apples are tender but the pan is dry, 10-15 minutes. Cool completely (spreading on a parchment-lined sheet pan speeds this up).
Spread the cooled apple filling evenly over the baked crust, pressing gently to close any gaps. Break the reserved walnut topping into pebble-sized pieces and scatter or arrange over the filling.
Bake until the topping is golden brown, 45-50 minutes. Cool completely in the pan on a rack, then lift out using the foil, slide off, and cut into 24 bars (6 strips one way, 4 the other).

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup/114 grams unsalted butter (1 stick), softened, plus more for coating dish
ingredients.item: unsalted butter (1 stick), softened, plus more for coating dish

ingredients.rawText: 4 tablespoons/50 grams granulated sugar, plus more for coating dish
ingredients.item: granulated sugar, plus more for coating dish

ingredients.rawText: 8 ounces/225 grams bittersweet chocolate (60 to 65 percent cacao), finely chopped
ingredients.item: bittersweet chocolate (60 to 65 percent cacao), finely chopped

instructions.text: Remove the oven racks and set a baking sheet directly on the oven floor. Heat oven to 400°F. Generously butter a 1 1/2-quart soufflé dish, then coat the bottom and sides with sugar and tap out the excess, making sure sugar covers all the buttered surface for the best rise.
Melt the chocolate and butter together (microwave or over a pot of simmering water). Let cool only slightly, so it's still warm, then whisk in the egg yolks and salt.

With an electric mixer, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar at medium speed until fluffy with very soft peaks. Add the sugar one tablespoon at a time, beating until the whites hold stiff, glossy peaks.

Whisk about a quarter of the egg whites into the chocolate mixture to lighten it, then fold in the rest in two additions. Transfer to the prepared dish and run a thumb around the inside edge to create a 1/4-inch gap between the dish and the batter.

Set the dish on the hot baking sheet in the oven and lower the temperature to 375°F. Bake until puffed and the center barely moves when shaken, 25-35 minutes (don't open the oven door for the first 20 minutes) — less time for a runnier center, more for firmer. Serve immediately.

instructions.text: Spread the cornstarch on a plate or rimmed sheet pan and toss with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Coat both sides of the tofu slices in the mixture, shaking off the excess, and set aside.

Heat a large (12-inch) skillet over medium-high for 2 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon oil and the broccoli, season with salt and pepper, and cook, tossing, until just tender, 3-5 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.

Keeping the heat on medium-high, add 2 tablespoons oil to the skillet. Cook half the tofu in a single layer until golden, 2-3 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and cook the rest of the tofu the same way.

Lower the heat to medium. Add the butter, gochujang, soy sauce, maple syrup, garlic and ginger, and cook until the butter melts. Stir in 3 tablespoons water and cook until the sauce thickens slightly, 1-2 minutes. Add the tofu and broccoli back in and gently toss to coat.
Top with the scallions and sesame seeds, and serve with rice.

3/4 cup/170 grams unsalted butter (1 1/2 sticks), melted and cooled
ingredients.item: unsalted butter (1 1/2 sticks), melted and cooled

ingredients.rawText: 1 cup/200 grams granulated sugar (for lemon layer)
1/4 cup/30 grams all-purpose flour (for lemon layer)
1/8 teaspoon fine sea salt (for lemon layer)

instructions.text: Combine the cranberries, sugar and 3 tablespoons water in a medium saucepan. Zest 2 of the lemons directly into the pan and set the zested lemons aside.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, and continue boiling until the berries burst and the mixture turns jammy, 7-9 minutes. Remove from the heat and set aside.
Heat oven to 350°F. Line a 9-by-13-inch baking pan with a single large sheet of heavy foil with no gaps, then coat generously with cooking spray.

Whisk the flour, sugar and salt for the crust in a bowl. Whisk the vanilla into the melted butter, then pour over the flour mixture and stir until it comes together. Press into an even layer in the pan and bake until golden around the edges and dry on top, 17-20 minutes.
While the crust bakes, squeeze the juice from the 2 zested lemons (about 1/2 cup); squeeze another lemon if needed to reach that amount.
Whisk the sugar, flour and salt for the lemon layer in a bowl. Add the eggs and whisk gently just until incorporated, then stir in the lemon juice just until smooth.
Let the baked crust cool 5 minutes, then spread the cranberry mixture evenly over it. Slowly and carefully pour the lemon mixture on top to form two distinct layers.

Bake until the filling is set, 18-22 minutes. Cool completely in the pan on a rack, then refrigerate until cold and firm, at least 2 hours. Lift out using the foil, cut into 24 squares (wiping the knife between cuts), and dust with powdered sugar if desired just before serving.

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy pot over medium-high. Add the ground beef, onion and celery, and cook, breaking up the meat, until it's no longer pink and the vegetables start to soften, 5-7 minutes. Stir in the garlic and cook 2 minutes more.

ingredients.item: blueberries, washed, drained and picked over

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Cream the butter and sugar until light.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then add the vanilla.
Sift together the flour, salt and baking powder, and add to the creamed mixture alternately with the milk.

Line a 12-cup standard muffin tin with cupcake liners and fill with batter. Sprinkle the 3 teaspoons of sugar over the tops and bake at 375°F for about 30-35 minutes.

ingredients.rawText: 3 cups/385 grams all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting

ingredients.rawText: 1 cup/225 grams unsalted butter (2 sticks), softened
1 large egg, at room temperature, plus 1 egg white
ingredients.item: egg, at room temperature, plus 1 egg white

ingredients.rawText: 1/4 cup/50 grams coarse black sanding sugar (optional)

instructions.text: Whisk the flour, salt and baking powder together in a bowl and set aside. Coat a small loaf pan with cooking spray, then line it with plastic wrap, tucking it into the corners with plenty of overhang.

In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream the butter and confectioners' sugar on medium-high until fluffy, 2-3 minutes. Add the egg and vanilla and beat on medium-high until combined, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl as needed.
Add the flour mixture and beat on low until combined, then increase to medium and beat until the dough starts to clump together.

Turn the dough out, knead lightly, and form into a log. Cut into two pieces, one about 1/3 and the other about 2/3 of the dough. Beat the plain tahini into the larger piece until fully combined and set aside. Beat the black tahini into the smaller piece until fully combined.

On a well-floured surface, cut the white dough in half and pat half into a 5-inch square. Cut the black dough in half and pat half on top to match. Repeat with the remaining dough so you have four alternating layers. Cut in half crosswise, gently knead and roll each half to marble the colors together, then stack and briefly knead the two pieces into one soft dough.

Press the dough into the prepared loaf pan and fold the plastic wrap over the top to seal, pressing to even out the surface. Chill until firm — preferably overnight, or at least a few hours (up to 3 days ahead, or freeze up to 3 months).

Heat the oven to 325°F. Beat the egg white with 1 teaspoon water. Spread the sanding sugar on a small baking sheet. Unmold the dough, trim the sides square if desired, lightly brush the outside with the egg white mixture, then roll and press it in the sugar to coat all sides except the ends.
Cut the block into barely 1/4-inch-thick slices and lay them 1 inch apart on parchment- or silicone-mat-lined baking sheets. Freeze until firm, about 10 minutes.
Bake until golden underneath, 14-16 minutes. Cool a few minutes on the sheets, then transfer to wire racks to cool completely. Keeps in an airtight container at room temperature up to 1 week.

instructions.text: Combine the mirin and sake in a small saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil 20 seconds without boiling off too much liquid, then lower the heat and whisk in the miso and sugar, stirring over medium heat until the sugar dissolves (don't let it boil). Remove from heat and whisk in the sesame oil, then let cool and transfer to a wide glass, stainless steel bowl, or baking dish.
Pat the fish fillets dry, brush or rub with the marinade on both sides, and place in the dish, turning a few times to coat. Cover and marinate 2-3 hours, or up to a day.
Light the broiler or prepare a grill. Line a sheet pan with oiled foil. Tap each fillet against the dish to let excess marinade drip off; place skin side up on the sheet pan if broiling.

Grill skin side down, or broil skin side up, about 6 inches from the heat, 2-3 minutes per side until browned and blackened in spots. If needed, finish in a 400°F oven about 5 minutes more, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.

instructions.text: In a small saucepan over high heat, boil the sugar with 1 cup (240 ml) water, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Reduce to a simmer, add the lemon juice and extract, and simmer until thickened into a syrup, about 2 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool.

Pour the yogurt mixture over the semolina mixture and mix well. Transfer to the buttered dish and press into an even layer. Score the surface on the diagonal into 2-inch diamonds and top each diamond with an almond. Bake until golden brown, 25-30 minutes.
Set the dish on a wire rack and drizzle the cooled syrup over the hot cake. Let cool to room temperature before recutting along the scored lines and serving.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, cold and cut into cubes

Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface, gather into a ball, and flatten into a disk with the heel of your hand. Wrap tightly in plastic and refrigerate at least 1 hour and up to 2 days.

ingredients.item: cauliflower, about 1 medium-large head, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices or 2-inch florets

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Put the cauliflower in a large bowl, pour on enough olive oil to coat (a few tablespoons), season generously with salt and pepper, and toss gently until evenly coated.

Spread the cauliflower on a baking sheet and drizzle any remaining oil from the bowl on top. Bake, turning once, until caramelized at the edges and tender, 25-30 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature as a side dish; a splash of good aged vinegar is nice on top.

Garnish with parsley before serving.

instructions.text: Combine the chicken thighs, salsa verde, green chiles, garlic, jalapeño, garlic powder, onion powder and cumin in a 6- to 8-quart slow cooker and stir to combine evenly (don't add salt yet, since jarred salsas are often high in sodium). Cook on low until the chicken is tender and the flavors meld, 5-6 hours. (If you'll be away 8+ hours, set the cook time to 4 hours on low and let the auto-switch to warm handle the rest.)

Shred the chicken coarsely with two forks. With the heat still on low, stir in the scallions and cilantro. Season to taste with salt and lime juice, then serve with rice or in tortillas with your choice of accompaniments.

instructions.text: Combine the yogurt, cucumbers, chopped mint and garlic in a medium bowl and mix well. Chill until ready to serve.
In a second bowl, mix the beef, onion, turmeric, 1 teaspoon of the salt and plenty of black pepper until well combined.

Heat a large well-seasoned cast-iron skillet (or other heavy-bottomed pan) over medium-high. Once very hot, break the beef into large, irregular chunks with two spoons or your hands and drop into the skillet. Cook undisturbed until charred and crisp on the bottom and browned partway up the sides, 6-8 minutes.

With a wooden spoon, toss the meat and break up any large pieces. Add the walnuts and raisins and continue cooking, stirring often, until the meat reaches your desired doneness and the walnuts are toasted, 2-3 minutes more.

Take the yogurt from the fridge and season with the remaining teaspoon of salt. Spread it on a serving platter, top with the crispy meat, drizzle with pomegranate molasses if using, and garnish with mint leaves. Serve with warmed pita or rice.

instructions.text: Combine 2 teaspoons ground cumin, the chile powder and 1 teaspoon salt. Cut shallow crosshatched incisions across the top and bottom of the steak, then rub the spice mix all over it (gloves recommended, the chile powder is hot). Place the steak in a resealable freezer bag.

Whisk together the lime juice and zest, 1/4 cup olive oil, the Worcestershire sauce and half the garlic. Reserve 2 tablespoons of this marinade and pour the rest into the bag with the steak. Seal, coat thoroughly, place on a sheet pan and refrigerate at least 4 hours and up to 24, massaging the bag occasionally. Refrigerate the reserved marinade too if cooking the next day.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large, heavy skillet over medium-high. Add the onion and cook, stirring, until softened and starting to color, 4-5 minutes. Stir in the bell peppers and chile and cook, stirring, until the peppers begin to soften, about 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining garlic and cumin, and salt to taste. Cook, stirring often, until the peppers are nicely seared, softened and starting to caramelize, 5-8 minutes.
Pour in the reserved 2 tablespoons of marinade and scrape up the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Stir in half the cilantro, taste and adjust seasoning, then remove from heat but keep warm.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm in a low oven, or wrap in a towel and warm in a steamer or the microwave.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high, or prepare a medium-hot grill. Remove the steak from the marinade (discard the marinade) and pat dry. If using a skillet, heat the remaining tablespoon of oil (cut the steak in half and cook in batches if it doesn't fit). Cook 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil, for 10 minutes, then slice across the grain into 1/2- to 3/4-inch strips.

Arrange the lettuce on a platter and place the sliced steak next to it. Pour any accumulated juices from the cutting board over the meat and sprinkle with the remaining cilantro. Serve the vegetables on the same platter or separately, along with warm tortillas, salsa and crumbled queso fresco.

instructions.text: Heat the broiler. Warm the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed soup pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the minced garlic and red pepper and let sizzle 30 seconds without browning. Add the mussels, stir to coat, and raise the heat to high. Add the wine or water and cover. After 2 minutes, stir the mussels, replace the lid, and continue cooking until all the mussels have opened, 6-8 minutes.
Brush the cut sides of the baguette pieces with oil and toast cut-side up under the broiler. Rub the toasts with the remaining garlic cloves.
Stir the chopped parsley into the mussels, then ladle the mussels and broth into bowls. Serve with the garlic toasts.

instructions.text: Butter a 13-by-9-inch baking pan and line with buttered parchment paper. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Melt the butter, chocolate and both sugars together in a double boiler over barely simmering water, or in a microwave on low power, and let cool slightly. In a large bowl or mixer, whisk the eggs, then whisk in the salt and vanilla.

Whisk the chocolate mixture into the eggs. Fold in the flour just until combined, then stir in the chopped walnuts if using. Pour the batter into the prepared pan; if using whole walnuts, arrange them on top of the batter. Bake 35-40 minutes, until shiny and beginning to crack on top. Cool in the pan on a rack.

8 ounces/225 grams bittersweet chocolate, coarsely chopped into chunks

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Coat a 9-by-13-inch pan with nonstick spray and line with parchment, leaving 2 inches of excess on the long sides to help lift the blondies out later.

If using whole graham crackers, pulse them in a food processor (or crush in a bag with a rolling pin) into a fine powder. Add the flour, baking powder and salt to the crumbs and pulse a few times to combine.

In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, cream the butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar on medium until light and fluffy, 4-5 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each and scraping the bowl.

Mix in the vanilla. On low speed, add the graham crumb mixture and mix just to combine. Mix in about 3/4 of the chocolate. Transfer the dough to the prepared pan and press into an even layer with damp hands.

Bake on the lower rack until golden at the edges with a crackly surface, 30-32 minutes. Remove from the oven, sprinkle the marshmallows evenly over the top, and return to the upper rack. Bake until the marshmallows soften and turn golden brown, 6-8 minutes.

Remove the pan. If any marshmallows have puffed up, pop them with a toothpick or skewer (they deflate easily). Sprinkle the reserved chocolate over the top and return to the upper rack; bake until the chocolate is melted and the marshmallows lightly toasted, about 2 minutes. Cool on a rack for 45 minutes.
Run a thin knife between the blondies and the pan on the short sides, then lift out using the parchment sling. Cool 10 more minutes, then slice into 12 pieces and serve.

Drain the noodles, rinse with cold water, drain again, and toss with a splash of sesame oil.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tablespoons sesame oil, the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame paste, peanut butter, sugar, ginger, garlic and chile-garlic paste.
Pour the sauce over the noodles and toss to coat.
Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with the cucumber and peanuts.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F. Combine the flour, baking soda and salt in a small bowl. In a large bowl, beat the butter, granulated sugar, brown sugar and vanilla until creamy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Gradually beat in the flour mixture, then stir in the chocolate chips and nuts if using. Drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased baking sheets.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 325°F. Butter and flour a 12-cup Bundt pan. In a small bowl, combine 3 tablespoons of the bourbon with the candied ginger and let stand 10 minutes.
In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the brown sugar and butter on medium-high until light and fluffy, about 5 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time until incorporated.

In a separate bowl, whisk the flour with the baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, salt and nutmeg. In another bowl, whisk together the sour cream and vanilla; pour in the bourbon from the ginger mixture (reserving the ginger) and whisk until smooth. Whisk in the zest.

With the mixer on medium, add the dry mixture and the sour cream mixture to the wet mixture in three additions, alternating between the two. Fold in the ginger, apples and pecans. Scrape the batter into the prepared pan. Bake until golden brown and a skewer comes out dry, about 1 hour 10 minutes. Cool in the pan 20 minutes, then run a paring knife around the edges to release; cool flat side down on a wire rack.

While the cake cools, combine the granulated sugar and the remaining 1/2 cup bourbon in a small saucepan. Warm gently over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then stir in the lemon juice and remove from heat.

While the cake is still warm, poke 10 slits on top with a paring knife and pour half the bourbon-sugar glaze over it. Once the cake is fully cool, flip it, pour the rest of the glaze on the other side, then flip again to serve.

instructions.text: Prick the eggplant with a thin-blade knife. Grill over or next to very high heat, turning as necessary, until the skin blackens and the eggplant collapses — or broil, or roast on a heated cast-iron pan in the hottest possible oven. Takes about 20 minutes.
Once the eggplant is cool enough to handle, peel it (this should be easy) and trim away the hard stem. Chop or mash it in a bowl with the lime juice.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and add the onion. Cook, stirring often, until golden brown, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic and chile and cook another minute. Add the tomato, turmeric and salt, and cook until the tomato is soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the mashed eggplant and cook, stirring, 3-5 minutes. Stir in the cilantro and garam masala and turn off the heat. Serve hot with warm chapati bread or pita, or over rice.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F/190°C. Grease a 9- or 8-inch/21-centimeter loaf pan with butter, line with a parchment paper sling, and butter the paper. Set aside.

In a stand mixer with the paddle attachment, beat the butter, sugar, lemon zest and vanilla on high for 3-4 minutes until light, then lower to medium. Add the eggs in three additions, scraping the bowl as needed — the mix may split a little but it will come back together once the dry ingredients go in.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, salt and almond flour. With the mixer on low, add the dry ingredients in three additions, mixing just until no white specks remain. Fold in about 3/4 of the blueberries by hand, then scoop the batter into the prepared pan.

Cover loosely with foil and continue baking another 25-30 minutes (less for a 9-inch pan, more for an 8-inch) until risen and a knife comes out clean. instructions.text: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring and swirling the pan often, until it foams, turns golden brown and smells nutty, about 5 minutes. Pour into a large bowl and let cool.

ingredients.item: scallions, trimmed and cut on a sharp bias into thin, 2-inch-long pieces

instructions.text: Prepare the tofu: cut into 3/4-inch cubes and put into a bowl. Bring a kettle of water to a rolling boil. Turn off the heat and when the boiling subsides, pour hot water over the tofu to cover. Set aside for 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large wok or skillet over medium heat, toast the peppercorns for 2-3 minutes, until super fragrant and slightly darkened (a wisp of smoke is normal). Let cool briefly, then pound with a mortar and pestle, or pulse in a spice grinder.

Set a strainer over a measuring cup, then add the tofu to drain; reserve 1 1/2 cups of the soaking water, discarding the rest. Set the tofu and reserved soaking water near the stove with the peppercorns and other prepped ingredients for swift cooking.
Reheat the wok or skillet over high. When hot, swirl in the oil to evenly coat, then add the meat. Stir and mash into cooked and crumbly pieces, 1-2 minutes.

Add 2 1/2 tablespoons doubanjiang, the douchi (if using), ginger and red-pepper flakes (if using). Cook about 2 minutes longer, stirring constantly, until things are vivid reddish brown. Add the soy sauce and sugar, stir to combine, then add the tofu. Gently stir or shake the pan to combine without breaking up the tofu much.
Add the reserved 1 1/2 cups soaking water, bring to a vigorous simmer, and cook for about 3 minutes, agitating the pan occasionally, to let the tofu absorb the flavors of the sauce.
Slightly lower the heat and taste the sauce. If needed, add the remaining 1/2 tablespoon of doubanjiang for heat, a pinch of salt for savoriness, or a sprinkle of sugar to tame heat.

Add the scallions and stir to combine. Stir in the cornstarch slurry, adding enough to thicken to a soupy rather than gravy-like finish. Sprinkle in the ground peppercorns, give the mixture one last stir to incorporate, then transfer to a shallow bowl. Serve immediately with lots of hot rice.

instructions.text: Put the oil, butter and chopped onion in the pot and turn the heat on to medium. Cook and stir the onion until it has become translucent, then add the chopped celery and carrot. Cook for about 2 minutes, stirring vegetables to coat them well.

Add milk and let it simmer gently, stirring frequently, until it has bubbled away completely. Add a tiny grating (about 1/8 teaspoon) of nutmeg, and stir.

Add the wine, let it simmer until it has evaporated, then add the tomatoes and stir thoroughly to coat all ingredients well. instructions.text: Make the cookies: In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour and baking soda. In a large bowl, stir the matcha and vanilla into a paste using a wooden spoon or flexible spatula. Add the butter, peanut butter, granulated sugar, brown sugar and salt, then beat until pale green and fluffy. Switch to a whisk and beat in the egg until smooth.
Add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients and fold until just combined. Refrigerate the dough, uncovered, while the oven heats.
Heat oven to 350 degrees. Line a couple of baking sheets with parchment paper.

Using a #40 (1 1/2-tablespoon) cookie scoop or two spoons, scoop out 1 1/2-inch rounds and place them a couple of inches apart on the baking sheets. Bake until puffed and no longer wet-looking on top, about 12 minutes. Let the cookies cool completely on the pan. (Unfrosted cookies can be stored in an airtight container for 2 to 3 days.)

If you'd like, make the frosting when you're ready to serve the cookies: in a medium saucepan off the heat, whisk together the granulated sugar, flour and salt. Whisk in the milk until smooth. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until the mixture starts to bubble, about 4 minutes, then continue whisking as it boils until thick like pudding, about 2 minutes longer. Transfer this hot mixture to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment.

ingredients.rawText: 2 large firm eggplants, cut into 1/2-inch slices

instructions.text: Heat broiler and line a baking sheet with foil or parchment.

Brush both sides of eggplant slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon salt. Arrange slices on the prepared baking sheet and broil in batches until deep mahogany brown, turning once halfway through, 5 to 7 minutes per side.
Adjust the oven to 375 degrees with a rack positioned in the center.

In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of the remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add onion and sauté until translucent but not browned, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Add ground lamb or beef, stirring frequently and breaking up the meat into very small pieces with the side of a metal spoon. Season with remaining teaspoon salt, cinnamon and pepper. Sauté until meat is just cooked through. Taste and add more salt or pepper as needed.

In a medium skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add pine nuts and reduce heat to medium-low. Stir nuts to coat them with butter and continue stirring constantly until golden brown, 2 to 4 minutes, watching closely since they can burn quickly once they begin to brown. Transfer nuts to a bowl while still warm and salt them lightly.

Coat a 13-by-9-by-2-inch baking dish with the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Spread 1/2 cup of tomato sauce in the bottom of the dish. Lay 1/3 of the eggplant slices in a single layer over the sauce, covering as much surface area as possible. Spoon half the meat evenly over the eggplant. Pour 1/3 of the remaining tomato sauce evenly over the meat. Sprinkle with 1/3 of the pine nuts. Layer again with eggplant, meat, tomato sauce and pine nuts. Finish with a layer of eggplant and cover with more tomato sauce, sprinkling the top with pine nuts.

Pour 1 cup warm water around the perimeter of the baking dish (the sauce will thicken as it bakes). Cover the pan with foil and bake for 90 minutes. Remove foil and top the eggplant evenly with mozzarella. Bake 15 minutes longer, uncovered, or until the cheese is bubbling and golden. Serve warm, over rice.

instructions.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Pat pork chops dry and, using a very sharp paring knife, cut a large pocket into the fat-covered edge of each chop. Season chops all over with 1 teaspoon salt, including inside the pockets.

Stir in the chili powder and cook until fragrant, just a few seconds. Add the ground turkey, season with salt and stir to combine, breaking up the meat with the spoon. (Don't worry about browning or cooking it through here, as it will do so when it simmers.) Stir in the reserved liquid from the tomato can.

Use the fork to fish out as many chipotle peppers from the can as you would like, starting with two or three, and add to the pot, breaking them up with the wooden spoon, along with all of the adobo sauce. The more peppers you use, the spicier your final chili will be; if you like spice, just add the entire can. (Store any peppers you don't use in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to a week and in the freezer for up to 2 months.) Fill the empty chipotle can with cold tap water, swish it around and add to the pot. Stir to combine.

Bring the chili to a simmer over medium-high heat — you should see occasional small bubbles breaking the surface of the mixture — then cover the pot and reduce the heat to continue simmering over medium-low, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has reduced and the tomatoes have broken down, about 20 minutes. The chili should look thick and shiny, but not too thick that you couldn't ladle it into a bowl. (If it's too watery, then simmer with the lid off for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.) Taste and add more salt if desired. Serve with cheese, sour cream and cilantro, if using.

instructions.text: In a bowl, cover chickpeas by at least 2 inches of cold water. Add 1 teaspoon baking soda and let soak at room temperature overnight. Drain and rinse.

(Overcooked chickpeas are the secret to creamy hummus, so don't worry if they start to break down a little.) Drain.

While chickpeas are cooking, make the tahini sauce. In a blender, combine the lemon juice, garlic and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Let mixture sit 10 minutes. Add tahini, remaining 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and the cumin, and blend until a thick paste forms. Add 1/3 to 2/3 cup ice water while blender is running, a little at a time, until sauce is smooth. Add the warm, drained chickpeas to blender with tahini mixture. Blend until perfectly smooth and not at all grainy, stopping to scrape down sides of bowl occasionally. This blending may take upward of about 2 minutes; just keep going until the mixture is ultracreamy and fluffy, adding a little water if you need it to make the contents of the blender move. For homemade paneer (makes 12 ounces): line a large colander with a double layer of cheesecloth and set it in the sink. In a large wide pot, bring the milk to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring frequently to avoid burning the bottom.

instructions.text: Make the light soaking syrup first, since it needs to cool to room temperature before using. In a medium saucepan, combine the sugar, water and squeeze of lemon juice. Set over medium-high heat and gently stir as it heats, avoiding sugar granules up the sides of the pan, until the sugar dissolves completely. Bring to a full boil, then remove from heat immediately. Set aside to cool completely.

Make the heavy sugar syrup: in a small saucepan, combine the sugar, water and drop of lemon juice. Set over high heat, avoiding stirring to prevent crystallization. Once it boils, reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, or until the syrup thickens and reduces to 100g (1/3 cup).
Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 210°C/410°F. Grease a 34cm (13-inch) round pan with ghee; set aside.
In a medium bowl, combine the semolina and melted ghee, stirring well with a rubber spatula to coat every grain of semolina — this reduces gluten formation, which is what can make a basbousa tough.
If desired, process the coconut in a food processor or spice grinder until very fine. Stir into the semolina/ghee mixture until well combined.

In a microwave-safe measuring cup or small bowl, combine the milk, heavy sugar syrup, and sugar. Heat in the microwave until very warm, about 1 1/2 minutes. Whisk well until the sugar is fully dissolved (test by rubbing a bit between your fingers — it should feel gritless).
Pour the warm milk mixture over the semolina mixture and, using a rubber spatula, fold gently just until no dry pockets of semolina remain. Do not overmix, or the basbousa can turn tough.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan. Tap the pan on the counter several times to smooth out.
Refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes to rest (no longer than 1 hour), until the batter has thickened and no longer jiggles. Sprinkle the nuts, if using, over the surface, pressing in to adhere.
Bake for 22 to 27 minutes, or until the surface is deep golden brown.

As soon as the basbousa comes out of the oven, quickly pour the cooled light soaking syrup all over it. It should soak in within a few minutes. Once soaked in, brush the surface with 2 tablespoons of ghee, if desired.

Allow to cool in the pan for at least 30 minutes before cutting into squares and serving. Serve warm or at room temperature with fresh eshta if desired. Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week at room temperature.

ingredients.rawText: 1 pound mushrooms such as cremini or white, halved lengthwise if large
ingredients.item: mushrooms such as cremini or white, halved lengthwise if large

ingredients.rawText: 3 tablespoons unsalted butter, cut into pieces

instructions.text: Preheat oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Toss mushrooms with capers, garlic, oil, 1/8 teaspoon salt and several grinds of pepper in a 1 1/2- to 2-quart shallow baking dish.
Top with butter and roast, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender and golden and a bubbly garlic sauce forms below, 15 to 20 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice and parsley. Serve immediately, with crusty bread on the side for swiping up the juices.

ingredients.item: white wine, or more to taste

instructions.text: Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium heat until brown on all sides, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove from skillet, and slice.

Melt butter in the same skillet. Stir in onions and garlic, and cook 2 to 3 minutes. Mix in bell peppers, season with basil and oregano, and stir in 1/4 cup wine. Continue to cook and stir until peppers and onions are tender, 5 to 7 minutes.
Return sausage slices to the skillet. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes, or until sausage is heated through, adding more wine if needed.
Serve hot.

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup rice (any short to medium grained variety) - 100 grams
ingredients.item: rice (any short to medium grained variety)

ingredients.rawText: 1/3 cup moong dal (husked and split mung lentils) - 85 grams
ingredients.item: moong dal (husked and split mung lentils)

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup jaggery, chopped and tightly packed - 115 to 120 grams
ingredients.item: jaggery, chopped and tightly packed (or jaggery powder)

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 cup water - for the jaggery syrup
5 green cardamoms or 1/2 teaspoon green cardamom powder

instructions.text: Pick over the rice and moong dal to remove any stones. Heat a small pan or kadai and add both the rice and moong lentils. On low heat, stirring often, roast both until aromatic — you don't need to brown them, just roast until fragrant. Transfer to another bowl and rinse both a couple of times with water.

Drain well and add both to a pressure cooker. Pour in 3 cups water (adjust depending on the consistency you prefer and the quality of the moong dal). Pressure cook on medium heat for 11 to 12 minutes, or 8 to 9 whistles.

Let the pressure settle down on its own, then remove the lid and check doneness. If the texture looks separate like a pulao, add 1/2 to 1 cup hot water and mix well. Both the rice and dal should be cooked well and look mushy — slightly mash with a spoon; the consistency should be like a khichdi. Cover and set aside.
Meanwhile, crush the seeds of 5 green cardamoms plus 1 clove in a mortar and pestle (or use 1/2 teaspoon cardamom powder alone).

Chop the jaggery to get about 1/2 cup tightly packed. In a pan, combine with 1/2 cup water and heat on low to medium flame, stirring and breaking up the jaggery, until it melts completely into an amber (or pale yellow, depending on the jaggery) syrup.

Strain the jaggery syrup through a fine mesh strainer directly into the cooked rice and lentils (or add jaggery powder directly if using). Add the crushed cardamom and clove powder and a pinch of edible camphor if using. Mix well — the mixture will thicken as it cools, so add 1/4 to 1/3 cup hot water or hot milk if it looks too thick.
Heat 4 to 5 tablespoons ghee. Add the cashews and sauté until light golden. Add the raisins and stir-fry until they swell and become plump.
Immediately remove the pan from heat and add the fried cashews, raisins and ghee to the cooked rice and lentils. Mix thoroughly. Serve sweet pongal hot or warm.

R0249.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against vegrecipesofindia.com / Dassana's Veg Recipes (Dassana Amit), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Variations: substitute jaggery with raw/white/palm/coconut sugar; use milk instead of water for a richer texture; equal parts rice and moong dal also work.

ingredients.rawText: 1/4 cup pine nuts, toasted (omit if following keto diet)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.

Arrange the eggplant halves cut side up in a large baking dish. Brush with two tablespoons of oil and sprinkle with some of the salt. Bake until the skin is browned and the flesh is soft, about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, in a large cast iron or non-stick skillet, heat the remaining one tablespoon of oil. Add the onions and garlic, season with salt and sauté over medium heat, stirring often, until softened.

Add the ground lamb and the spices. Brown, breaking up the meat with a wooden spoon, until cooked through, about 5-10 minutes. Stir in the crushed tomatoes and pine nuts, if using, reserving a tablespoon for topping.
Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Cut the eggplant down the middle, making sure not to tear the skin on the bottom. Spoon the lamb mixture onto the eggplants in the baking dish. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Garnish the eggplants with parsley and reserved pine nuts and serve immediately.

R0262.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against all-thats-jas.com (Jas, adapted from The New Mediterranean Table cookbook), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Note: pine nuts can be swapped for toasted almonds, walnuts, pistachio, or Panko for a nut-free version.

ingredients.rawText: 1 1/2 lbs Japanese Eggplant (about 4 x 10 inch eggplants)
1 teaspoon Szechuan peppercorns (or sub regular peppercorns)
1/4 cup soy sauce or low sodium soy sauce
ingredients.item: soy sauce or low sodium soy sauce

ingredients.rawText: 1 tablespoon garlic chili paste (or 1 teaspoon chili flakes)
ingredients.item: garlic chili paste (or 1 tsp chili flakes)

ingredients.rawText: 3 tablespoons sugar, brown sugar, coconut sugar, maple syrup or alternative
ingredients.item: sugar (or brown sugar, coconut sugar, maple syrup)

ingredients.rawText: Scallions and roasted peanuts (or Peanut Chili crunch), for garnish
ingredients.item: scallions and roasted peanuts (or peanut chili crunch), for garnish

instructions.text: Cut eggplant into 1/2-inch thick half-moons or bite-sized pieces. Place in a big bowl covered with water and stir in 2 teaspoons salt. Cover with a plate and let stand 20-30 minutes.

Meanwhile, chop the garlic and ginger and make the Szechuan sauce: toast the Szechuan peppercorns in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, then crush. Combine with the remaining sauce ingredients (soy sauce, chili paste, sesame oil, rice vinegar, Chinese cooking wine, sugar, and five spice) in a small bowl and whisk. Set by the stove.
Drain and rinse the eggplant and pat dry with a towel. Toss with the cornstarch.

Working in 2 batches, heat 1-2 tablespoons oil in an extra-large skillet over medium heat. Add half the eggplant, spreading it out, and let one side brown before turning with tongs. Take your time to get both sides golden and the insides cooked through — about 10 minutes per batch. Set the eggplant aside.
Add 1 more tablespoon oil to the skillet and, over medium heat, add the garlic and ginger, stirring for 2 minutes. Turn the fan on, add the dried chilies and stir for one minute.

Pour the Szechuan sauce into the pan and bring to a simmer for 20 seconds. Add the eggplant back into the skillet, tossing gently for about 30 seconds — don't over-reduce, or it will get salty. If it seems dry, add a tablespoon of water to loosen.
Place in a serving dish and top with scallions and optional peanuts. Serve with rice, cauliflower rice, black rice or rice noodles.

R0280.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against feastingathome.com (Sylvia Fountaine, 'Szechuan Eggplant' / Chinese Eggplant), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. The dried red chilies flavor the oil but are not meant to be eaten.

ingredients.rawText: 16 ounces ahi tuna, thawed (sushi-grade saku block)
1 tablespoon soy sauce or GF liquid aminos
ingredients.item: soy sauce or GF liquid aminos

ingredients.rawText: 2 tablespoons high heat oil for searing - peanut oil, wok oil, avocado
ingredients.item: high heat oil for searing (peanut, wok, or avocado oil)

ingredients.rawText: 3 tablespoons sesame seeds (black, or both black and white)
ingredients.item: sesame seeds (black, or both black and white)

ingredients.rawText: 1 teaspoon granulated garlic powder (or onion powder)

instructions.text: Mix the sesame crust ingredients together in a small bowl.
Pat dry the ahi tuna with paper towels. Place on a plate and coat all sides with soy sauce (this helps the sesame spice adhere).
Generously sprinkle all sides of the ahi tuna with the sesame mix, pressing it down into the flesh to coat.

Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until very hot (a flick of water should sizzle loudly). Turn the fan on high, add the oil, and let it get hot. Carefully lay the tuna in the pan, pressing it down with a metal spatula. Sear 45-60 seconds, checking the underside by lifting a corner — when deeply golden, carefully flip (if not golden, turn the heat up). Sear the other side 60-90 seconds until golden, then sear the long edges using tongs to hold it upright. The goal is a golden crust on all sides without cooking the tuna through.
Place on a cutting board and, using a very sharp knife, thinly slice and serve.

R0267.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against feastingathome.com (Sylvia Fountaine), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Note: can be refrigerated up to 3 days and served chilled. Serve with furikake rice and Asian cucumber salad.

ingredients.rawText: 250 gms unsalted butter (1 cup + 2 tbsp, approx @ room temp)
A small piece cinnamon (for spice powder)
A small piece nutmeg (for spice powder)

instructions.text: Soak the fruits: use a combination of sultanas, seedless raisins, currants and candied orange and lemon peel (or dried fruits of choice, chopped small if using dates/apricots). Soak in the rum/brandy for a minimum of 1 week (up to 1.5 months), shaking the jar occasionally.

Make the caramel: combine sugar and 1 tablespoon water in a saucepan. Heat and let the sugar melt until dark brown. Remove from heat and carefully add the warm water (it will splash). Return to heat and boil 3-4 more minutes. Remove from heat and cool completely.
Grind the spices with a pinch of sugar to a fine powder and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (355°F) for 10-15 minutes before baking.

Drain the soaked fruits, retaining 4 tablespoons of the liquor. Toss the drained fruits in 1-2 tablespoons of flour to prevent sinking. Sift the plain flour with baking powder and baking soda. Powder the sugar. Separate the egg yolks and whites; beat the whites to soft peaks and set aside.

Beat the egg yolks with the softened butter until a smooth paste forms. Gradually add the powdered sugar, beating after each addition. Once smooth, add vanilla essence, cooled caramel, and spice powder, and beat again.
Add the sifted flour in 2 batches, beating after each addition. Add jam and combine.
Fold in the beaten egg whites in 2 parts, combining until no white streaks remain. Fold in the soaked fruits and the 4 tablespoons of retained liquor.
Grease the baking dish and line with baking paper. Pour the batter into the prepared tins. Bake in the preheated oven for 40-45 minutes, or until a skewer inserted comes out clean.

R0285.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against mariasmenu.com (Maria Jose), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Alcohol-free version: soak the 3 cups of fruit in 1.5 cups fresh orange juice overnight at room temperature instead of rum. Notes: light brown sugar can substitute for more color; store at room temp in an airtight container up to 2 weeks, or refrigerate up to a month.

ingredients.rawText: 2 small or 1 large onion (2 cups sliced)

instructions.text: Cut peeled onions in half from pole to pole. Using a mandolin or very sharp knife, slice onions into very thin strips, approximately 1/16 inch thick.
Place onions on a microwave-safe plate or pie plate, add olive oil and salt, and stir with a fork to coat the onions thoroughly. Distribute onions in an even layer on the plate.

Microwave uncovered on high for a total of 12 to 13 minutes (based on a 1100 watt microwave; adjust as needed), stirring after 4 minutes, 8 minutes, and each minute after that. Each time you stop, use two forks to pull apart clumps and redistribute the onions evenly. After minute 8, watch closely, as they can go from browned to burnt quickly. Stop as soon as they are evenly cooked, browned, and crispy (a few burnt bits are okay).
Cool completely and store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week.

R0293.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against theyummylife.com (Monica Matheny), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Great as a topping for green bean casserole, roasted vegetables, sandwiches, scrambled eggs, soups, or Indian biryani.

ingredients.item: tomato, chopped and ground to a paste

ingredients.item: freshly ground black pepper powder, or to taste

ingredients.rawText: Homemade Garam Masala : 1/2 tsp (or store bought : 1/4 tsp)
Fennel Seeds/Perum Jeerakam : 1 tsp (for homemade garam masala)
Cinnamon Stick/karugapatta : 2 inch piece (for homemade garam masala)
Green Cardamom/elakka : 2 pods (for homemade garam masala)

instructions.text: If making homemade garam masala: dry roast the fennel seeds, cinnamon, cloves, star anise, and green cardamom, then grind to a fine powder and set aside.
Clean and wash the chicken pieces with turmeric powder and drain.
Marinate the chicken for 30 minutes to 1 hour with the marination ingredients and set aside.

Heat 1 tablespoon of coconut oil in a pan; add a few curry leaves followed by crushed ginger and crushed garlic, and sauté for a couple of minutes. Add finely chopped shallots (or onion) and green chillies; sauté over medium-low heat until translucent.

Add coriander powder and turmeric powder, sauté for a minute. Add the ground tomato paste along with a couple tablespoons of water, and cook until the tomatoes are cooked and most of the water has evaporated.
Add the marinated chicken, mix well so the pieces are coated with masala, adjust salt, and cook covered for about 20 minutes without adding water.

Uncover and cook uncovered for another 10 minutes. Add freshly crushed black pepper powder, homemade garam masala, grated coconut, and 1 sprig of curry leaves. Combine well and cook on low flame until the chicken pieces are dry and light brown, stirring occasionally to avoid burning, about 10 minutes.
Add 1 tablespoon of coconut oil and dry roast, uncovered, until browned.

Once the chicken meat starts to fall apart and has attained a dark brown color, remove from heat. Keep covered for 10-20 minutes to let the flavor set. Serve with steamed rice, roti, appam, or Indian bread.

R0306.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against kothiyavunu.com (Sangeetha), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. This is a spicy dish — adjust black pepper to taste; fresh ground pepper and coconut oil are recommended for authentic flavor.

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Wash and slice the potatoes into 1-inch pieces. Slice the kielbasa into medallions. Dice the onion into 1-inch pieces.

Add the potatoes, kielbasa, onion, and frozen green beans (no need to thaw) to a large baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle the steak seasoning over top. Use your hands to toss until everything is coated in oil and spices.
Transfer the baking sheet to the oven and roast for 20 minutes, then give the ingredients a good stir. Roast for an additional 15 minutes, or until browned to your liking. Serve hot.

ingredients.rawText: 4 cups chicken stock/broth (or water/half water half stock, for lower sodium)
ingredients.item: chicken stock/broth (or water, or half water half stock)

ingredients.rawText: 1 package Japanese curry roux (7-8 oz or 200-230 g)
8 servings cooked Japanese short-grain rice, for serving
ingredients.item: cooked Japanese short-grain rice, for serving

ingredients.rawText: Fukujinzuke (Japanese red pickled vegetables), for serving (optional)
ingredients.item: fukujinzuke (Japanese red pickled vegetables), for serving (optional)

instructions.text: Cut the onions into wedges (or mince/thinly slice if you prefer them to disintegrate into the sauce). Peel the carrots and cut into rolling wedges (rangiri cut). Peel the potatoes, cut into quarters, and soak in water for 15 minutes to remove excess starch. Grate the ginger; mince the garlic. Cut the apple into quarters, remove the core, peel, then grate it. Trim excess fat from the chicken thighs and cut into bite-sized pieces (diagonal sogigiri cut recommended). Season with black pepper.

Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and add the onion. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until translucent and tender, about 5 minutes (a few extra minutes for more caramelization and flavor is worth it if you have time).
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and mix well. Add the chicken and cook, stirring frequently, until no longer pink on the outside. Reduce heat if the onions are browning too much.
Add the chicken stock/broth. Add the grated apple, honey, soy sauce, and ketchup.

Add the carrots and potatoes; the broth should barely cover the ingredients. Simmer, covered, on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Once boiling, skim the scum and foam from the surface with a fine-mesh strainer. Continue to cook covered until a wooden skewer passes easily through the carrots and potatoes.
Turn off the heat. Dissolve the curry roux 1-2 cubes at a time in a ladleful of the cooking liquid, stirring into the pot to incorporate, and repeat until all the roux is used.
Simmer uncovered on medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until the curry thickens, about 5-10 minutes (add water if too thick). Stir often so nothing sticks to the bottom and burns.
Serve the curry with steamed Japanese short-grain rice, garnished with fukujinzuke if desired.

R0367.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against justonecookbook.com (Namiko Hirasawa Chen), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Storage: refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze up to a month (remove potatoes before freezing, as texture changes).

ingredients.rawText: 1 pound small red and or yellow potatoes, halved (or quartered for larger potatoes)
ingredients.item: small red and/or yellow potatoes, halved (or quartered if larger)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Optionally line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Place the potatoes in a large bowl and add 1 1/2 tablespoons of olive oil, half of the sea salt plus half of the rosemary, and 1 tablespoon of minced garlic. Toss to fully coat.
Spread the potatoes on a large baking tray in an even layer and bake for 20 minutes.

In the same large bowl, combine the green beans with the remaining ingredients: 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon garlic, and the remaining sea salt and rosemary. Toss to coat and add to the tray with the potatoes, spreading everything out so there's minimal overlap.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are golden brown and everything is fork tender.
Garnish with black pepper to taste and fresh parsley.

R0384.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against foodwithfeeling.com (Brita Britnell), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased.

ingredients.rawText: 8 ounces (225 g) sage sausage or breakfast sausage, removed from casings
ingredients.item: sage sausage or breakfast sausage, removed from casings

ingredients.rawText: 1/4 cup (7 g) minced fresh sage leaves
1/4 cup (7 g) minced fresh parsley leaves
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.rawText: 1 pound (450 g) homemade or store-bought pizza dough

instructions.text: Melt 2 tablespoons (28g) butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage and mash with a stiff whisk or potato masher to break into fine pieces (no bigger than 1/4 inch). Cook, stirring frequently, until only a few bits of pink remain, about 8 minutes. Add onion, celery, garlic, and sage and cook, stirring frequently, until vegetables are softened, about 10 minutes. Add parsley and season to taste with salt and pepper. Transfer to a large bowl and set aside until completely cool.

While the filling cools, make the knots. On a lightly floured surface, divide the dough into 2 even pieces. Working with one piece at a time, roll or stretch into an oblong strip about 8 inches long and 4 inches wide. Cut crosswise into 12 strips with a bench scraper or knife. Repeat with the other half of the dough.

Tie each strip into a knot and transfer to the bowl with the sausage mixture. Toss and fold gently with your hands until every knot is thoroughly coated. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with 1 tablespoon (14g) butter. Transfer the knots to the dish in a single layer. Drizzle with olive oil, cover tightly with plastic wrap, and set aside until doubled in size, about 4 hours at room temperature (or 12 to 16 hours refrigerated). Alternatively, cover in foil and freeze up to a week, thaw completely in the fridge, then bring to room temperature for an hour before baking.
When ready to bake, adjust oven rack to center position and preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Unwrap the rolls and bake until golden brown and crisp, 25 to 30 minutes.
When the rolls are almost ready, melt the remaining tablespoon of butter. Remove the rolls from the oven and immediately brush on the butter. Serve with gravy and cranberry sauce on the side.

R0387.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against Serious Eats (J. Kenji Lopez-Alt), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Bacon, pancetta, or chorizo can substitute for the sausage; store-bought pizza dough works well here since the other flavorings are strong.

ingredients.item: sardines in tomato sauce with chili

ingredients.rawText: 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (or to taste)
ingredients.item: red chili powder, or to taste

instructions.text: Heat oil in a skillet and add the fenugreek seeds. When they begin to splutter, add the garlic paste followed by the chopped onion. Sauté the onion until golden brown.
Add the chopped tomatoes and all the dry spices (being careful with salt since canned sardines already contain salt). Cook on low-medium heat until the tomatoes are soft and oil oozes out.
Open the sardine cans and gently add the sardines along with the tomato sauce to the skillet. Avoid moving the sardines too much to prevent breaking the pieces.
Add the slit green chilies and simmer for about 5-7 minutes to heat the sardines fully and let the flavors mingle.
Garnish with chopped cilantro. Serve hot with boiled rice.

R0398.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against sadafsculinaryadventures.com (Sadaf Afshan), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. If using plain tomato sauce sardines instead of chili, increase the red chili powder to taste.

ingredients.item: drained cooked chickpeas (or 200g dried, soaked overnight then cooked)

ingredients.rawText: 2-4 green chillies, finely chopped, seeds and all
ingredients.item: green chillies, finely chopped, seeds and all

instructions.text: Put the drained chickpeas in a pan and add 500ml water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes, then drain, retaining the cooking water.

Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan over medium heat and, when hot, add the cumin seeds. Fry until aromatic, stirring, then add the onion and turn the heat down. Cook until golden brown, stirring regularly. Meanwhile, use a pestle and mortar or stick blender to mash the garlic, ginger, 25g of the fresh coriander, and chillies into a paste.

Add this paste to the pan and cook for a couple of minutes, stirring so it doesn't catch, then add the ground coriander, chilli powder and turmeric (with a splash more oil if necessary) and cook for a couple more minutes.
Stir in the mashed tomatoes, chickpeas and their cooking water, and salt. Bring to a lively simmer, then turn down the heat to medium-low and cook for 20 minutes, or until thickened.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, then allow to cool slightly before serving, scattered with the remaining coriander leaves.

ingredients.item: firm-ripe Bosc or Anjou pears (3 large), peeled, cored, cut into 8 wedges each

instructions.text: Combine 1/3 cup of the rum with the pears, water, raisins, sugar, and butter in a 10-inch heavy skillet. Bring to a boil, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat and simmer, covered, until the pears are just tender, about 10 minutes.
Remove the lid and boil, stirring occasionally, until the liquid reduces to a syrup, 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the remaining tablespoon of rum. Serve warm or at room temperature.

instructions.text: Chop the cauliflower into small florets, rinse well, and place in a bowl. Add enough hot water to cover the florets, then cover and blanch for 15-20 minutes.

Meanwhile, soak the dry red chilies in 1/4 cup warm water for 15 minutes. In a small grinder, blend the soaked chilies with the chopped garlic, chopped ginger, and 1-2 tablespoons water into a smooth paste.

Drain the blanched cauliflower well and transfer to a mixing bowl. Add the red chili paste and mix well, then add the gram flour, rice flour, and corn starch, followed by the turmeric, red chili powder, garam masala, and coriander powder.

Add the lemon juice and 1/3 cup water, then season with salt and mix everything together thoroughly. The batter should coat the florets without being runny or dry - adjust with a little more water or gram flour as needed. Cover and let marinate for 20-30 minutes.

Heat 7-8 tablespoons oil in a kadai or deep skillet until medium hot (about 350-356°F/175-180°C). Working in batches so as not to overcrowd, carefully place the battered florets in the oil and fry on one side until golden and crisp, then turn with a slotted spoon and fry the other side, turning as needed until evenly golden. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels.
For the tempering, remove excess oil from the kadai, leaving about 2 teaspoons (or use fresh oil). Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add the dry red chilies and fry until they darken.
Add the chopped onions, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves, and saute until the onions turn translucent. Season with salt and, if desired, a pinch of sugar to balance the heat.
Add the fried cauliflower florets and immediately switch off the heat. Toss to coat evenly, then stir in the chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with coconut chutney, coriander-mint chutney, or tomato ketchup, alongside roti or bread if desired.

R0437.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against vegrecipesofindia.com (Dassana Amit), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Original scan was a continuation card missing the first portion of the method, which is restored here.

ingredients.rawText: 1 pinch whole or powdered garam masala

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a pan and add the whole garam masala and cumin seeds. When they crackle, add the chopped onion, salt, and turmeric, and cook until the onion softens.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste, curry leaves, and chopped green chillies. Add the chopped tomato and cook for a few minutes until it softens.
Add the mushrooms and cook until they are soft and have released their moisture.
In a separate pan, melt the butter and add the crushed garlic, pepper, and cumin seeds. Stir in the coriander powder and cumin powder.
Add the cooked mushroom mixture to this spiced butter and cook, stirring, until the remaining moisture evaporates and the mushrooms are well coated.
Finish with the lemon juice and garnish with chopped coriander before serving.

Instructions paraphrased.

ingredients.rawText: 1 can (14 oz, 396 g) sweetened condensed milk
For the caramel: 1/2 cup (100 g) white granulated sugar
ingredients.item: white granulated sugar, for the caramel

ingredients.rawText: For serving: whipped cream, berries, mint leaves
ingredients.item: whipped cream, berries, mint leaves, for serving

instructions.text: Pour the condensed milk into a blender jar. Fill the same can with milk and add it to the blender, along with the eggs and vanilla. Blend for a few seconds and set aside.

To make the caramel, pour the sugar into a small saucepan over medium-low heat. As it begins to melt, stir with a rubber spatula, watching closely since sugar burns easily. Continue cooking and stirring until fully caramelized (light brown and melted).

Immediately pour the caramel into the flanera (flan pan). Using a potholder to hold the hot pan and a spatula, quickly spread a thin layer of caramel around the bottom and sides before it hardens. Let the remaining caramel pool and cover the bottom of the pan.
Blend the milk and egg mixture for about 10 more seconds to recombine, then pour it into the flanera over the caramel.

Seal the lid onto the flanera with its buckles. Place the sealed pan into a large baking dish and add water until it reaches about halfway up the flanera. Carefully place the baking dish in a preheated 350°F oven and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes. Remove carefully, as both the water and pans will be very hot.

Open the flanera and check for doneness: the flan is set when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. If it's still jiggly, return it to the oven's water bath for about 15 more minutes (it's better to slightly overcook than undercook, since an undercooked flan will fall apart when unmolded). Once done, remove the flanera from the water bath, let it cool completely, then refrigerate (still sealed) for at least 2 hours or overnight.

To serve, use a large plate with a lip to hold the caramel. Remove the lid, run a butter knife around the edge of the flan to loosen it, and twist the pan to confirm it moves freely. Place the serving plate on top of the flanera, then holding both tightly together, flip them over so the plate is on the bottom. Lift off the flanera so the flan sits in its pool of caramel on the plate.
Serve cold with a spoonful of caramel on each plate, topped with whipped cream if desired.

R0449.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against mariesaba.com (Marie Saba), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Serves 6-8; a sealed flanera (flan mold) baked in a water bath is used.

instructions.text: Heat oil in a frying pan. Fry the dry red chillies and keep aside. Fry the coriander seeds until fragrant and keep aside. Fry the black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and cumin seeds together and set aside. Stir-fry the pearl onions until browned.
Blend all the fried ingredients together in a mixer grinder.
Pressure cook the chopped mutton with the turmeric powder, salt, and the blended spice mixture.
In a separate pan, stir-fry the onions until browned, then add the green chillies, crushed garlic, ginger, and chopped tomatoes.
Add this to the cooked mutton and boil well until the curry turns brown, then turn off the heat.
Garnish with curry leaves, coriander leaves, and a spoon of coconut oil. Serve hot with rice.

ingredients.rawText: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon Madras curry powder
Basmati rice and warm naan, for serving
ingredients.item: basmati rice and warm naan, for serving

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a large enameled cast-iron casserole. Season the lamb with salt and cook over high heat, stirring occasionally, until browned, about 12 minutes. Transfer to a plate with a slotted spoon.
Add the onions to the casserole and cook over moderate heat until lightly browned, about 4 minutes. Stir in the ginger, garlic, curry powder, turmeric, cayenne, and bay leaves and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomato puree, yogurt, and water; bring to a boil and season with salt.
Return the lamb and any accumulated juices to the casserole. Cover partially and simmer over low heat until the lamb is very tender, about 1 hour.
Stir in the garam masala and cook for 5 more minutes. Discard the bay leaves, garnish with cilantro, and serve with rice and naan.

Turn the heat down to medium-low and stir in the coriander, cumin, cayenne, turmeric, ground toasted cumin seeds, amchoor (if using), paprika and garam masala. Cook the spiced onions for a minute or two, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and their juices, scraping up any browned bits stuck to the pan. Stir in the water and the chickpeas.
Simmer uncovered for about 10 minutes to let the flavors come together, then stir in the salt and lemon juice before serving.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick spray.
Whisk the flour, cocoa powder, baking soda and salt together in a medium bowl and set aside.
In a large bowl, mash the bananas well, then stir in the melted butter and oil. Mix in the brown sugar, egg and vanilla until smooth.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients just until combined - don't overmix. Stir in 3/4 cup of the chocolate chips.
Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and scatter the remaining 1/4 cup chocolate chips over the top.
Bake 50 to 65 minutes, checking at 50 minutes, until a toothpick comes out mostly clean (a little melted chocolate is fine, but avoid gooey batter).
Cool the bread in the pan on a rack for 15 minutes, then run a knife around the edges and turn it out. Let it cool until just slightly warm before slicing.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the center.
Set the salmon skin-side down in a baking dish sized to fit it snugly (about 8x12 or 9x13 inches), and season both sides with salt and pepper.

Stir together the mayonnaise, chile crisp, honey and lemon zest in a small bowl, tasting and adjusting with more chile crisp for heat or honey to mellow it. Spread the mixture evenly over the top of the salmon.

Bake until the thickest part flakes easily with a paring knife and the topping is bubbling a bit at the edges, 15 to 25 minutes depending on thickness. Spoon any glaze that has run off back over the fish before serving.

R0450.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against NYT Cooking (Naz Deravian), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Roasting one large fillet rather than several small ones makes the topping easier to spread and bakes more evenly.

4 cups cooked white rice, preferably leftovers

Sliced cucumbers or pickles, for serving (optional)

instructions.text: Season the salmon all over with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium-high and sear the fillets skin-side down until the skin is browned and crisp, 2 to 5 minutes, letting the color creep up the sides as the flesh turns from orange to pale coral. Once the flesh near the pan starts to feel firm rather than wobbly, transfer the salmon to a plate and set the pan (with its fat) aside.

Add the rice to the fat left in the pan, spreading and pressing it into an even layer like a rice pancake. Cook over medium heat, undisturbed, until the bottom is browned and toasted, about 5 minutes, then flip it in sections with a spatula and toast the second side for another 1 to 2 minutes (longer if you like it extra crispy).
While the rice cooks, stir together the gochugaru, maple syrup, rice vinegar and 1 teaspoon salt in a small bowl. Divide the toasted rice among plates.

In the same empty pan, add the gochugaru mixture and cook over medium-high, stirring constantly, until it bubbles and reduces to a sticky glaze, 15 seconds to 1 minute. Off the heat, whisk in the cold butter until fully melted and glossy.
Spoon the glaze over the seared salmon and serve alongside the crispy rice, with sliced cucumbers or pickles if you like.

R0351.note: Ingredients and steps confirmed against NYT Cooking (Eric Kim), 2026-08-30; instructions paraphrased. Gochugaru freezes well, so it's fine to buy a larger bag.

instructions.text: Heat the oven to 450°F. On a rimmed sheet pan, whisk together the chicken broth, olive oil, lemon juice and kosher salt.
Toss the potatoes in the liquid to coat, then arrange them cut-side down in a single layer. Sprinkle with the oregano, if using.

Roast, flipping the potatoes halfway through, until fork-tender and deeply browned and crisp on top, 55 to 60 minutes. If they're tender but not as crisp as you'd like, finish them briefly under the broiler.
Season with flaky salt and black pepper before serving.

instructions.text: Combine the fish, lime juice and onion in a glass or stainless-steel bowl, with enough lime juice to let the fish float somewhat freely. Cover and refrigerate about 20 minutes to a few hours, until a cube of fish no longer looks raw when broken open, then drain in a colander.

In a large bowl, mix the tomatoes, chiles, cilantro, olives and optional olive oil. Fold in the drained fish, then season to taste with salt (about 3/4 teaspoon) and the orange juice or sugar to soften the tang. Cover and refrigerate if not serving right away.
Just before serving, gently fold in the diced avocado without breaking up the pieces, and garnish with a few cilantro leaves. Serve with tortilla chips, tostadas or saltines.
